name: main-clock-and-setup-tests
goal: Unmodified main passes the loop-lifecycle command test on any date and the scoped-setup test matches the untagged svelte-kit sync step.

steps.title: Identify the failing behavior, expected behavior, and reproduction.
steps.evidence: On origin/main 4a321eb6c7 (2026-11-22), bun x vitest run test/loop-lifecycle.test.ts test/self-verify-config.test.ts: 2 failed. (1) loop list --stale 10 returned stale-open and fresh-open: the command reads the wall clock while fresh-open is seeded at 2026-11-12, so it went stale on 2026-11-22. (2) 4a321eb6c7 added an untagged svelte-kit sync setup step (needed by builds:[] scenarios whose root Vitest resolves generated package tsconfigs) without updating the scoped-setup expectation. The module-tasks managed-provider wrapper failure seen at 0ea7c34e3c was already repaired by #209 (251ac770bc) and passes.

steps.title: Explain why existing standardized tests missed the bug; name the scenario, fixture, lifecycle or assertion gap and reusable test change.
steps.evidence: The command test pinned no clock while every workflow-level test injects now(); the scoped-setup test hardcoded the setup list and nothing tied the config change to it. Reusable change: pin Date in command-level tests that compare fixture ages.

steps.title: Strengthen the existing standardized test; commit it before repair, run it failing with loop record --phase red, and preserve the assertion.
Implement the smallest repair without weakening the regression test.
Rerun the same unchanged regression test at a separate fix commit with loop record --phase green; preserve passing proof.
Run harness loop siblings to record the root cause and evaluate the same pattern across committed source.
Run relevant project checks and affected UI browser flows with fresh inspected screenshots and no unexpected browser errors; preserve diagnostics and keep pending until proof passes.
Both defects live in tests, so loop record cannot pair a test-only red with a product fix; record red, repair, green and guard commands here.
